The I.R.A.

I referred in my last report to the prosecution of three members of the Committee of Republican Unity, Nial Goold, Joseph O'Connor and Charles Smith. These men were tried before the Special Criminal Court on January 2nd 1946 and were found guilty of advocating and encouraging the formation and maintenance of an armed force not authorised by the Constitution and of being members of an illegal organisation. The first two were sentenced to twelve months imprisonment to terminate after six months if they entered into bail to keep the peace for two years. Charles Smith was sentenced to three months, not to take effect if he entered into bail to keep the peace for two years. A fourth man, Liam O'Reilly, was discharged - the State entering a nolle prosequi.

The charges arose out of speeches made at Cathal Brugha St. on September 9th 1946 when the defendants stated the objects of the Committee of Republican Unity, and made the usual extremist remarks.

From documents found by the police at Goold's residence in Iveagh Buildings it appears that the Committee of Republican Unity has fourteen Principles, the first of which is "as part of the international revolutionary working-class movement to do all in our power to preserve, defend and strengthen the Soviet State as the bulwark of the world proletariat".

The Principles go on to declare that in view of the world revolutionary events now taking place (the document was dated 5th May 1945) the demand for the Irish Republic must be put forward with increased vigour. By the Irish Republic is meant the Irish people united in arms and organised as the rulers of their own country. A seat on the World Security Organisation is to be demanded for the Irish Republic. The struggle for the Republic could not be carried on through the Labour Party as that Party collaborated with the State which can never grow into the Irish Republic. The main struggle must be carried on outside the Labour Party with the forces of both Communist and non-Socialist Republicans who have never accepted the Irish Free State. All economic struggles must be subordinated to the main political struggle.
